title: patch-surgery-cheats-and-untangle-map-leo
content:
Purpose:
This is a quick, intentionally messy scratchpad for patch-surgery techniques I want to try on PR #2489. The PR touches the KV cache invalidation path and a couple of hotpath branches; risk is medium-to-high because this code runs on dedicated GPUs and touches the streaming path.

High-level goals:
- Make the smallest possible change that fixes the regression reported in production traces (latency spike when cache-miss patterns align).
- Keep changes reversible and well-scoped for canary/rollback.
- Document quick tests and telemetry additions to catch regressions early after merge.

Immediate hypotheses (from trace + code skim):
1) A new conditional introduced in cache_lookup() can serialize on the LRU lock when requests have identical prefixes (rare but amplified by batching).
2) A new allocation path in kv_store.fetch_chunk might do a small sync on CUDA stream; combined with batching and cross-stream evictions, this leads to micro-blocks.
3) The new failure-path added for missing-tombstones triggers a slow fallback that wasn't instrumented (so we don't see it in logs, only in p99 latency).

Patch-surgery approach (order of preference):
A) Add observational telemetry only (no behavioral change) — short canary, get better signals.
B) If telemetry confirms hypothesis (A->true), introduce a non-invasive fix behind a feature flag and release to canary only.
C) If (B) fails or causes instability, revert and attempt alternative minimization (reduce batch-size on the affected route) before more invasive code changes.

Quick checklist for each attempt:
- [ ] Create branch pr/2489-surgical-obs-<initials> and reference INF-1123.
- [ ] Add: timer + counter around cache_lookup critical region (prefer microsecond histograms, sample at 1/1000 to avoid noise).
- [ ] Add: allocation counters for kv_store.fetch_chunk (size buckets), mark synchronous vs async paths.
- [ ] Wire new metrics to the internal canary dashboard (per-model, per-route).
- [ ] Smoke test locally with unit harness (simulate identical-prefix concurrency).
- [ ] Canary deploy to dedicated-small (5% traffic) for 1 hour.
- [ ] Verify p50/p90/p99 and collector counts, then escalate to 25% if stable.

Minimal code snippets to try (notes to self):
- Observability wrapper (pseudo):
  auto t0 = clock::now();
  bool lock_taken = try_rd_lock(lru_lock);
  // increment: metric.inc("cache.lock.attempt");
  // if lock_taken: metric.inc("cache.lock.acquire");
  ... original body ...
  metric.hist("cache.lock.latency_us", micros_since(t0));

- Non-invasive fallback behind flag (pseudo):
  if (feature_flag("kv-inplace-alloc-slowpath-fix")) {
     // try a cudaHostAlloc or prealloc arena instead of per-chunk alloc
  } else {
     // original path unchanged
  }

Safety gates and tests:
- Unit: simulate 200 concurrent requests hitting same prefix; assert no >2x baseline lock acquisitions.
- Integration: run existing streaming e2e with batcher scale=10, run latency checker for 30 mins.
- Regression: ensure tokenization and state machine outputs unchanged for N=100 deterministic prompts.

Fallback strategies if a small change fails:
1) Revert the telemetry-only branch (should be zero-risk, but be ready).
2) Throttle batcher for affected route (lower burst to 6 tokens/batch) via runtime flag — very low-risk but regresses throughput.
3) As last resort, revert the entire PR and open a follow-up to rework allocation model with attention from infra.

Communications plan (short):
- Ping @Maya in Slack with a short summary and link to canary dashboard before rollout.
- If canary shows any p99 increase, immediately mute traffic: run the automated rollback script (infra/ops-runbook).
- Post-mortem: short 48h note in INF-1123 if we revert or take >3 hours to stabilize.

Follow-ups and polish (post-fix):
- Extract a small deterministic test into the repo that reproduces the problematic interleaving (so future PRs can't reintroduce).
- Add a short doc in /docs/observability/cache-internals.md about the new metrics and how to interpret them.
- Consider a gradual refactor to reduce the critical region in cache_lookup: move eviction bookkeeping off the hot path into an async sweeper.

Open questions / TODOs for PR review:
- Q1: Does try_rd_lock add any ABI or portability concerns on the platforms we run (bare-metal + containerized GPUs)? (ask @Rina)
_notes_for_indexing: scratchpad; contains temporary branch names, monitoring plan, and quick pseudo-code for instrumentation and minimal fix. Focused on KV cache path and allocation behavior; intended for short-lived use until INF-1123 resolved.
